full_judgment: 4. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations stated in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that Munshi Imamuddin Dewan was very old and wise person with exceptionally good health, both physical and mental. A devout Muslim who till the last day of his life rarely failed to perform his five times daily prayers and also Tahazzud as well as other religious duties. He was a man of great integrity and character and of very independent spirit. During his long life not only brought up his children nicely, giving them good education but also acquired large landed property under P.S. Matlab, District-Chandpur in his own name and in the name of his children. Munshi Imamuddin Dewan also helped his son Md. Sadiq financially in acquiring property including suit land. Late Munshi Imamuddin Dewan used to live sometimes at his village home at Sengarchar under P.S. Matlab in Chandpur sometimes in the residence of defendant No. 1 and sometimes at Rajabazar with the family of late Md. Sadeq and sometimes with his younger son Nuruddin according to his own choice. He never liked to stay with any of his sons or daughter for a long time. After the death of Md. Sadeq, his wives and children did not like to stay with Imamuddin Dewan. Then the father of late Md. Sadiq left that place and went to the house of his daughter (defendant No. 1). The dependent No. 1 being a daughter received her father cordially and served him as best as she could. Munshi Imamuddin Dewan was not financially well of as his property yielded sufficient income. Munshi Imamuddin Dewan voluntarily and out of his deep affection for his daughter (defendant No. 1) expressed his willingness to transfer some of his property to the defendant No. 1. She agreed to accept such gift from her father. Accordingly Mushi Imamuddin Dewan on receipt of one volume of holy Quran made gift of 16 th share in the property in Schedule `A’ of the plaint with other properties to the defendant No. 1 and put the defendant No. 1 in ejmali possession of the property. Since then the defendant No. 1 has been in ejmali possession of the suit property on the basis of said gift. On the death of Md. Sadeq in the year 1977 Munshi Imamuddin Dewan became entitled to get 16 th  share of all his properties including land and buildings situated on C.S. Plot Nos. 110, 112, 113 of C.S. Khatian No. 24 described in the schedule `A’ of the plaint. Late Munshi Imamuddin Dewan had also 16 th share in the amount of Tk. 11,728.18 which was collected on the basis of succession certificate. In view of the fact that Munshi Imamuddin Dewan was entitled to 16 th share of the property of late Md. Sadeq, the property of Rajabazar comprising an area of 67 decimals of land worth of Tk. 60,00,000/- and share of Munshi Imamuddin Dewan would be valued at Tk. 10,00,000/-.
